name: Croatia
headline: SKIP THE *DUBROVNIK* QUEUE
intro: Three cruise ships dock and 8,000 people walk the same wall. There are 1,200 islands behind them and most have a ferry.

mustSee.name: Dubrovnik
mustSee.note: Go, but sleep there and walk the walls at eight. By eleven it's shoulder to shoulder.

mustSee.name: Plitvice Lakes
mustSee.note: The famous one, and genuinely worth it. First entry, and go anticlockwise against the flow.

mustSee.name: Split
mustSee.note: A Roman palace with a city living inside it. Diocletian's basement is still down there.

mustSee.name: Hvar
mustSee.note: Two towns and two completely different holidays. Stari Grad is the quiet one.

seasons.spring: May and early June. Sea is bearable, ferries are on the summer timetable, and Dubrovnik is walkable.
seasons.summer: July and August is the full experience — hot, packed and expensive. Book ferries weeks ahead or don't get on.
seasons.autumn: September is the best month on the coast. Warm sea, thinner crowds, and the island ferries still running properly.
seasons.winter: Most island places close entirely and the ferry timetable halves. Zagreb and the interior carry on as normal and are much better value.

transport: Buses do the coast better than trains — the railway barely touches it. Jadrolinija ferries and catamarans link the islands out of Split and Zadar; catamarans are faster but foot passengers only, so a car means the slow boat. A car is a liability inside the old towns and essential for Žumberak and the interior.
